implementation.existing_property: The one-phone activation was already one contiguous slice consumed by one suffix-down graph.
implementation.change: Enqueue the contiguous f32 activation upload asynchronously on the same CUDA stream as the suffix-down graph instead of synchronously uploading and synchronizing first.

effect.note: The asynchronous path removes an otherwise serial CUDA stream synchronization. The graph remains ordered after the upload on the same stream.

continuous_cadence.diagnosis: The gap penalty is primarily Android accessory-service wakeup on USB OUT, not slower HTP arithmetic.

phone_compute_profile.trace_diagnosis: Per-tile weight DMA intervals are approximately three to four times the HVX compute intervals. The M=1 q8 matmul is weight-bandwidth-bound.

controls.hmx_min1: correct but slower; native matmul about 411-412 us
controls.hvx_flat: failed correctness with zero phone activation
controls.op_fusion_toggle: no material benefit because gate and up are already stacked into one physical matmul

limits: This is one synthetic M=1 FFN layer, not a full-model token.
The treatment runs on a clock-reduced RTX A6000 transport host, not the physical RTX 4060 Ti.
Only one phone is present, so multi-phone concatenation and USB contention are not measured.
The split p90 remains above the CUDA-only p90 across the repeated aggregate.
No server, phone, link, or total-system energy acquisition was run.
next_phone_optimization: Batch independent activation rows so the q8 weights are reused across M and HMX becomes naturally eligible. Further M=1 compute-clock tuning is unlikely to help a weight-DMA-bound kernel.
